newsitem.title: UK: BAA shares boosted by CAA ruling.
newsitem.headline: BAA shares boosted by CAA ruling.

text.p: Shares in British airports operator BAA Plc advanced on Friday as investors cleared it for takeoff after yesterday's lenient pricing review by its regulator the Civil Aviation Authority, analysts said.
The price was up by 10-1/2p at 530p by 1045 GMT, adding to a 14-1/2p gain on Thursday.

Analysts said there was relief that the new price formula for regulated airline charges at London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports was not more demanding and the decision ended the months of uncertainty which has weighed on the share price all year.
"Relative to expectations earlier in the year it is as good as anyone could have realistically hoped for," said Guy Kekwick, London-based analyst at Lehman Brothers.

"The share price does have quite a lot of ground to catch up on but maybe now that we have got this regulatory review out of the way the market focus will turn back to the more positive aspects...such as the improving position in retail and continued growth in earnings, which has been forgotten for some time."
BAA was told on Thursday that it must cut airline user charges at London Heathrow and Gatwick by three percentage points below inflation every year for five years.

"The view is that the regulatory hurdle has been fairly successfully negotiated and we are looking at earnings and dividend growth averaging somewhere around 10 percent up to the next (five-yearly) review," said Rowan Morgan of Nikko Europe.
"What you have got here is fairly high quality visible earnings and I think it suggests we ought to be looking at a share price that rises to about 550p," he said.

The CAA said it had opted for a comparatively benign formula to encourage BAA to go ahead with its ambitious plans to build a huge new fifth terminal at London Heathrow at a cost of over 1.5 billion stg.
Were it not for Terminal Five the CAA said it would have imposed annual price cuts on the London airport charges of inflation minus eight percent to the year 2002.
BAA said the new formula was "workable" if challenging since it had wanted prices to be kept up in line with inflation.

But finance director Russell Walls said yesterday that regulated charges at the three regulated London airports, including the much smaller Stansted, amount to some 360 million stg a year, accounting for only 28 percent of the group's total revenues, of 1,253 million stg last year.

In comparison retail income was up 10.5 percent last year at 556 million stg, making airport shopping BAA's biggest single earner, and Walls said that figure was set to grow following a rapid expansion in airport shopping facilities.

Walls said another 200,000 square feet of retail space was likely to be added over the next five years but the main expansion programme was complete and the task now was to get passengers to spend more through new marketing initiatives.
Overall retail sales were up by over 10 percent in the first quarter this year with spend per passenger up by over 7.5 percent, he said.
